findings.text: the landed note cites "At 2a72458c" for runs whose counts that revision cannot produce — the isolation file holds 7 tests at 2a72458c while the note claims 8 passed there, and the three dispatch-arming logs name their own revision as 6d00c88d — so a reader checking the claim at the named revision finds a contradiction; the measurements are real but belong to the node's own tree or 6d00c88d.

the gate logs (serial-1..3, n4-1..7, attrib-1..2) open with pytest output and carry no revision, tree or command header, unlike the leak-* and dispatch-arming-* logs in the same run, so no gate log states the revision it ran at and a reader must infer it from mtimes and the manifest to attribute the recorded result.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit; 6d00c88d adds the session check with the registered-home helper and a discrimination test, 6d813b38 rewrites the two isolation assertions onto the home-bound scan and adds producers_naming_home beside the teardown path, and the plan (+37) and archive (+98) are pure appends with zero deletions, so both cumulative records gain their anchored section and lose nothing.
item_verdicts.done_when: each leg carries a receipt I opened — the deliberately leaked producer failed the session naming pid and home (logs/leak-detected.log, "pid 2036229 (RECKON_HOME=/tmp/pytest-of-mcintos/pytest-scratch-pos/test_a_deliberately_leaked_pro0/leaked-home)", exit 1); the declared negative control is recorded with its survivor (logs/leak-unreported.log, exit 0 while the producer stayed alive as pid 2038580, so the pass was a miss); both named files pass per file (logs/dispatch-arming-run1..3.log record 6 passed each, and my re-run of the isolation file at 6d813b38 passed 8, EXIT=0); and no reckon/ path is changed (git diff --numstat lists tests/ and docs/ only). The literal clause "every configuration home under the pytest base temp directory" is met in substance rather than in letter: two homes must sit outside that root, because the guarded code's own definition of an ordinary home is outside it, and the evidence record's scope note states the deviation instead of leaving it unstated.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is that no crew watch producer a test started survives the test session, and both halves land — the session fixture reads every live producer from /proc after the reaper and fails the session on one naming a test-owned home (tests/conftest.py:167), and the isolation file registers the throwaway homes it creates so a producer naming either is attributable (tests/test_watch_arming_isolation.py:235 and :307).
item_verdicts.manifest: read; its commits, test commands and result counts match the logs I opened (serial-1..3 at 34 passed; n4-1/2/6/7 green and n4-3/4/5 failing only on ids in files outside this node's scope, with attrib-1 reproducing the 5.0s bound failure without this node's files), one earlier unlisted per-file run (logs/final-test_crew_dispatch_arming.log, 02:33, a flock BlockingIOError in recovery.unwatch) is superseded by the three listed runs and named in neither the manifest nor the evidence record.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the declared paths are tests/conftest.py, tests/test_watch_arming_isolation.py, the plan HTML, the cumulative evidence HTML, and the figures directory; `git diff --name-only 2a72458c..6d813b38` returns exactly those, with the two new figure files inside the declared directory.

justifications.durability: each added assertion names the regression that reddens it — reinstating the arming suppression fails tests/test_watch_arming_isolation.py:184 through producers_naming_home, and widening or narrowing the scan's home predicate fails :381-382 — but the fixture's own fail wiring at tests/conftest.py:167 is exercised only by the run's scratch-test control logs and no committed test would catch its removal, so that follows the control logs rather than the suite.
justifications.evidence: the controls are two-sided and the receipts are real (logs/leak-detected.log names the pid and home; logs/leak-unreported.log proves the miss with the survivor alive; my re-run at the reviewed head passed 8), but the gate logs carry no revision, tree or command header and the plan's citation names a revision that cannot produce the stated counts, so the revision a result belongs to rests on the manifest rather than on the log.
justifications.fit: the helpers follow the module's existing idiom (module-level constants at tests/conftest.py:36, underscore-private functions with mechanism docstrings, and the local "from tests.conftest import" pattern already present at tests/test_watch_arming_isolation.py:304), no added line carries a plan, sprint or ticket label, and a collect-only at head lists exactly the 8 plus 6 intended items, so the test_-prefixed helper is not collected as a phantom test.
justifications.goal_fidelity: tests/conftest.py:167 makes a leaked producer fatal and names it by pid and home, and the registered-home helper at tests/conftest.py:222 keeps the isolation fixtures attributable; the one place the goal is not absolute is a producer naming a home outside the base temp directory with a prefix no test registered, which the run's own follow_on records as needing the merged-head full-suite confirmation rather than claiming it here.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --numstat 2a72458c..6d813b38 shows all six changed paths inside the declared list (both HTML files pure additions, zero deletions), nothing outside it, and no reckon/ file touched.
